Keywords of QTrans_run

Structure of the input data

We use a yaml file as the input configuration. For different cal_mode values, the program requires different input blocks. However, the parameters in basic block must always be defined in the input file. The format is as follows:

basic:
    cal_mode: <cal_mode>
    graph_data_path_uc: <graph_data_path_uc>
    nao_max: <nao_max>
    Ham_type: <Ham_type>
    outdir: <outdir>

block_name1:
    key1: value1
    key2: value2

block_name2:
    key3: value3
    key4: value4

Keywords

cal_mode, graph_data_path_uc, nao_max, Ham_type, outdir

Block <advanced>:

Block <phonon>:

Block <epc>:

grad_mat_path, mat_info_sc_path, cell_range_cut, phonon_frequency_cutoff, LRC_taylor_order, q_cut

Block <transport>:

k_size, q_size, bands_indices, fermi_maxiter, fermi_shift, temperature, smeark, smearq, gauss_type, e_thr, is_hole, mode_resolved

Block <conductivity>:

phonon block

supercell_matrix
Options: *LIST[LISTS[FLOAT, FLOAT, FLOAT]]*
Default: None

Specifies the \(3 \times 3\) matrix used to construct the supercell from the unit cell for phonon calculations with the Phonopy package.

phonon

Back to top

unitcell_filename
Options: *STRING*
Default: './POSCAR'

The unit cell POSCAR file used for phonon calculations with the Phonopy package.

phonon

Back to top

force_infos_filename
Options: *STRING*
Default: './FORCE_SETS'

Path to the phonon force data loaded by Phonopy. Supported inputs are extensionless text FORCE_SETS or FORCE_CONSTANTS files, force-constant files ending in .h5 or .hdf5, and Phonopy .yaml files containing the required structure and force data.

For text inputs, the first line distinguishes FORCE_SETS (one field) from FORCE_CONSTANTS (two fields). These files are read using the default VASP unit convention: displacements in angstrom, forces in eV/angstrom, and force constants in eV/angstrom squared. A filename does not identify or convert units. See Phonon Force Data Preparation for the workflow and the conversion required for ABACUS-generated force sets.

phonon

Back to top

apply_correction
Options: True | False
Default: False

If True, the system is treated as polar, and the non-analytic correction to the phonon frequencies is included. In addition, the dipole contribution to the long-range electron-phonon coupling matrix elements is included.

phonon

Back to top

quadrupole_correction
Options: True | False
Default: False

Controls whether the long-range dynamical quadrupole contribution is included in the electron–phonon coupling matrix elements. When set to True, QTrans reads the dynamical quadrupole tensors from Q_file. This parameter can be set independently of apply_correction. Enabling both parameters includes the long-range dipole and quadrupole contributions; enabling only quadrupole_correction includes the quadrupole contribution alone.

phonon

Back to top

Q_file
Options: *STRING*
Default: './quadrupole.fmt'

Specifies the path to the dynamical quadrupole tensor file. The file is read only when quadrupole_correction is True. The structure of Q_file is:

atom  dir    Qxx      Qyy      Qzz      Qyz      Qxz      Qxy
1     1      ******   ******   ******   ******   ******   ******
1     2      ******   ******   ******   ******   ******   ******
1     3      ******   ******   ******   ******   ******   ******
2     1      ******   ******   ******   ******   ******   ******
2     2      ******   ******   ******   ******   ******   ******
2     3      ******   ******   ******   ******   ******   ******
......

****** represents a quadrupole-tensor component.

The file should contain a header beginning with atom, followed by \(3 \times N\) consecutive data rows, where \(N\) is the number of atoms in the unit cell. Each atom occupies three rows corresponding to displacements along the Cartesian x, y, and z directions (dir = 1, 2, 3). Atoms must appear in the same order as in the unit cell used for the calculation. Value of the quadrupoles is in units of \(e \cdot \mathrm{bohr}\). Quadrupole tensors can be obtained using ABINIT software.

phonon

Back to top

BECs
Options: *LIST[LISTS[LISTS[FLOAT, FLOAT, FLOAT]]]*
Default: None

The Born effective charge used for long-range corrections in polar system. Should be a \(\text{number_of_atoms} \times 3 \times 3\) tensor.

phonon

Back to top

DL
Options: *LIST[LISTS[FLOAT, FLOAT, FLOAT]]*
Default: None

The dielectric constant matrix used for long-range corrections in polar system. Should be a \(3 \times 3\) matrix.

phonon

Back to top

thickness
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 0.0

The effective thickness used for long-range corrections in 2D polar system.

phonon

Back to top

chiral_projection
Options: True | False
Default: False

If True, the phonon eigenvectors will be projected onto XY-chiral phonon modes.

phonon

conductivity block

over_band_edge
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 0.2

Specifies the energy cutoff (in eV) for selecting electronic states. For metals, it is the half-width of the window around the Fermi level. For semiconductors, it is the energy extent into the conduction band from the CBM, or into the valence band from the VBM. This selection limits the states included in transport-related calculations.

conductivity

Back to top

MC_sampling
Options: 'none' | 'uniform' | 'Cauchy'
Default: 'none'

Specifies the type of importance sampling used in Monte Carlo integration.

  • none: No importance sampling.

  • uniform: Uniform random sampling.

  • Cauchy: Cauchy-distributed sampling, which emphasizes sampling near singularities.

conductivity

Back to top

polar_split
Options: 'none' | 'polar' | 'rmp'
Default: 'none'

Specifies whether to separate the polar and non-polar contributions to the scattering rate.

  • none: No splitting is applied.

  • polar: Computes only the polar (long-range) part of the scattering rate.

  • rmp: Computes only the remainder (non-polar) part.

See theory/Electron Phonon Coupling for more details.

conductivity

Back to top

cauchy_scale
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 0.035

The scale parameter \(\gamma\) of the Cauchy distribution used for importance sampling. This is only effective when MC_sampling: cauchy.

The probability density function is given by:

\[f(x) = \frac{1}{\pi} \cdot \frac{\gamma}{x^2 + \gamma^2}\]

where \(\gamma\) is the scale parameter.

conductivity

Back to top

sampling_seed
Options: *INT*
Default: 1

Random seed used for Monte Carlo sampling to ensure reproducibility.

conductivity

Back to top

nsamples
Options: *INT*
Default: 1000000

The number of sampling q points in the Monte Carlo integration. This is effective for both MC_sampling: cauchy and MC_sampling: uniform; it is unused for regular-grid sampling.

conductivity

Back to top

ncarrier
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 10000000000000000.0

The carrier concentration in \(\mathrm{cm}^{-3}\) for a three-dimensional system, or \(\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\) when advanced.system_2D: True.

conductivity

Back to top

mob_level
Options: 'erta' | 'ibte'
Default: 'erta'

Specifies the method used for electrical conductivity calculation.

  • erta: Self-energy relaxation time approximation.

  • ibte: Iterative Boltzmann Transport Equation approach.

See theory/Conductivity Calculation for more details.

conductivity

Back to top

polar_rate_path
Options: None | *STRING*
Default: None

Path to the precomputed scattering rate file for the polar part of the interaction.

conductivity

Back to top

rmp_rate_path
Options: None | *STRING*
Default: None

Path to the precomputed scattering rate file for the remainder (non-polar) part of the interaction.

conductivity

Back to top

epc_rate_path
Options: None | *STRING*
Default: None

Path to the precomputed total scattering rate file.

conductivity
scattering_channel_dir
Options: None | *STRING*
Default: None

Path to the folder containing the precomputed scattering channels required for iterative Boltzmann transport equation calculations.

conductivity

Back to top

ibte_error
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 0.00001

Absolute convergence threshold for the iterative Boltzmann Transport Equation (IBTE). The maximum change in tensor components between consecutive iterations is compared with this value: conductivity in S/m for metals, or mobility in \(\mathrm{cm}^2/(\mathrm{V}\,\mathrm{s})\) for semiconductors. This parameter is only effective when mob_level: ibte.

conductivity

Back to top

ibte_cycle
Options: *INT*
Default: 200

Maximum number of iterations allowed in the IBTE calculation loop.

conductivity

breakdown block

fbd_erange
Options: *LIST[FLOAT, FLOAT, FLOAT]*
Default: [0.0, 1.0, 0.01]

Specifies the energy range and step (in eV), given as [min, max, step], over which the breakdown properties will be calculated. The energy is referenced to the conduction band minimum.

breakdown

Back to top

fbd_rate_file
Options: None | *STRING*
Default: None

Path to a previously generated QTrans breakdown rate file. If not None, the scattering and energy-loss rates are read from this file instead of being recomputed.

The file must have six whitespace-separated columns: ik_ibz, ibnd, weight_k, enk, scattering_rate, and energy_loss_rate. Indices are zero-based and must match the current irreducible k-point ordering and band selection. Energy and rates use internal atomic units: Hartree, Hartree, and Hartree squared, respectively (with atomic time and hbar = 1). Comment lines start with #. Duplicate index pairs are rejected; omitted states remain unavailable.

Reuse a file only with compatible structures, bands, k-point grids, temperature, phonon data, and broadening settings. Older files expressed in eV, 1/ps, and eV/ps require unit conversion before reuse.

breakdown

Back to top

fbd_effective_mass
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 1.0

The electron effective mass (in \(m_\text{e}\)) in intrinsic breakdown field strength formula.

breakdown

Back to top

fbd_exp_bandgap
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: 0.0

The band gap value (in eV) in intrinsic breakdown field strength formula.

breakdown

resistivity block

ziman_nc
Options: *FLOAT*
Default: -9999.9

Number of charge carriers per unit cell used in Ziman’s resistivity formula. If set to a negative value, QTrans will automatically estimate it based on the number of band crossings at the Fermi level. This is a heuristic estimate, not a carrier-density integral. Zero is invalid because this quantity enters the denominator of the resistivity formula.

resistivity

Back to top

omega_range
Options: *LIST[FLOAT,FLOAT]*
Default: [0, 100]

Specifies the energy range (in meV), given as [min, max], over which the Eliashberg spectral function \(\alpha^2 F(\omega)\) and the Eliashberg transport spectral function \(\alpha_{tr}^2 F(\omega)\) will be calculated.

resistivity

Back to top

omega_step
Options: *INT*
Default: 200

Specifies the energy step (in meV) used for calculating the Eliashberg spectral function \(\alpha^2 F(\omega)\) or the Eliashberg transport spectral function \(\alpha_{tr}^2 F(\omega)\).

resistivity

Back to top

self-energy block

SE_type
Options: 'electron'
Default: 'electron'

Specifies the quasiparticle type of which the self-energy will be calculated.

self-energy

Back to top

SE_mode_resolved
Options: True, False
Default: False

Added 2026-10-23. Save the complex electron self-energy contribution from every phonon branch in <outdir>/self_energy/electron_self_energy_modes.npz. This option is independent of transport.mode_resolved.

Requires cal_mode: band, disp_renormalize: True, band_grid_mode: False, SE_type: electron, sparse gradients, magnetic_type: none, soc_switch: False, and both phonon long-range correction flags set to False. Unsupported combinations are rejected from the original input, before workflow-specific overrides.

All 3 * natoms branches are saved after the q sum and electronic degeneracy average. Existing total self-energy and spectrum formats are preserved. The NPZ is created exclusively; use a new output directory for each run.

self-energy

Back to top

SE_erange
Options: *LIST[FLOAT,FLOAT,FLOAT]*
Default: [0.0,0.0,0.0]

Specifies the energy range (in eV), given as [min, max, step], over which the spectral function will be calculated.
